transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-04-08
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Li (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (Harbor - Head of Platform), Rajesh Iyer (Harbor - SecEng), Mei Chen (Harbor - CTO)
Shared links: Redwood SOC2/ISO (redwood.com/security/soc2.pdf), security brief deck (link shared in chat)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on Harbor's security posture requirements for choosing between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment. Main topics: SOC2/ISO attestations, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data retention and residency. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send attestation docs and run a Dedicated perf pilot; Harbor to provide retention policy and sample data.

Topics:
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II, ISO27001
- Identity & Access: SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM, RBAC
- Auditability: audit logs, access logs, query logs, export windows
- Encryption: at-rest encryption, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), key rotation
- Data residency & retention: region-specific storage, minimum/maximum retention windows, purge/eraser requirements
- Deployment tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (networking, latency, control, cost)

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): All right, hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Sofia, AE on the Redwood team, and with me is Marco, our security/perf SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Alicia (Harbor): Good, thanks. We wanted to go through our security checklist for inference workloads — SOC2, SSO, KMS stuff.
[00:13] Marco (Redwood): Great; we can walk through each item and map to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private options — and call out what we typically provide out of the box vs enterprise add-ons.
[00:22] Mei (Harbor): High level — Harbor's evaluating hosted first but we may need Dedicated or Private for data residency and key control. We're sensitive to PHI-ish telemetry and some regulated telemetry from our customers.
[00:33] Rajesh (Harbor): And we need details around audit logs and retention; our compliance team will want immutable logs for 7 years for some records.

[02:05] Marco (Redwood): On attestations, Redwood has SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 — we can share the reports. For Hosted, we have contractual commitments on data handling; Dedicated gives you dedicated pools and stronger isolation; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you the most control, including direct network peering and customer-managed KMS.
[02:34] Sofia (Redwood): I'll drop the SOC2 and ISO certs after the call — short link in the chat. Note that some customers start Hosted and then move to Dedicated for throughput and KMS.

[04:12] Rajesh (Harbor): For KMS, does Redwood support customer-managed keys in Hosted? We require that keys be rotated by us and not accessible by vendor ops.
[04:20] Marco (Redwood): For Hosted we offer envelope encryption and integrate with major cloud KMS providers; we also support Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted BYOK, there are extra controls — typically we provision a customer KMS namespace or use a KMIP/HSM integration depending on the cloud region. There can be a slight increase in lat due to key unwrap calls, we can measure that in the pilot.
[04:48] Alicia (Harbor): So hosted BYOK is available but with some constraints — we'd need to see the exact KMS flow and who has access to key material.
[05:03] Marco (Redwood): Exactly. We'll share the KMS integration doc and a diagram.

[07:10] Sofia (Redwood): On SSO and SAML — Redwood supports SAML 2.0, OIDC, and SCIM provisioning for user sync. For RBAC we have role templates plus custom roles; you can map SAML attributes to roles.
[07:38] Mei (Harbor): Do you support enforced MFA, conditional access, and session timeouts from our IdP?
[07:45] Marco (Redwood): We surface session length configuration and honor assertions from the IdP; conditional access policies are enforced at the IdP level, and we respect those session claims. For more advanced device posture checks you may need Private where you can place an auth proxy.

[09:20] Rajesh (Harbor): Auditability — how granular are audit logs? We need to show who invoked model endpoints, payload hashes, timestamps, and admin changes. And retention — can logs be exported to our SIEM?
[09:33] Marco (Redwood): Logs include request metadata, user identity (subject), model/version, IPs, and admin actions. We provide streaming export to customers' S3 buckets or to SIEM via syslog/forwarders. For Hosted we retain standard logs for 90 days; Dedicated/Private customers can configure longer retention and export.
[09:58] Alicia (Harbor): 90 days won't fly for us. We need at least 2 years on some logs and 7 years for a subset. Can you support that?
[10:07] Marco (Redwood): Yes, with Dedicated/Private we can arrange custom retention policies and long-term archival to your S3 with lifecycle policies. We'll need to scope storage costs. We'll also provide redacted audit bundles for audits.

[12:45] Sofia (Redwood): A common approach is Hosted for non-sensitive workloads and Dedicated/Private for regulated workloads. It sounds like Harbor may run initial eval on Hosted for dev and then Dedicated for prod with custom retention and KMS.
[13:05] Mei (Harbor): That matches our thinking. One nuance: latency-sensitive endpoints must be <120ms p50 and p95 target under our peak loads; can Dedicated guarantee that?
[13:16] Marco (Redwood): We have SLA tiers and Dedicated can be sized to meet your p95 latency with reserved capacity. We'll run a perf bench using your sample payloads — that'll show realistic latency and cost.
[15:00] Rajesh (Harbor): Legal will want data residency clauses. Do you support region locking and geo-fencing?
[15:07] Sofia (Redwood): Yes. For Hosted we have region-specific endpoints; Dedicated/Private gives you full control over which region the data resides in. We'll capture the exact regions Harbor needs.

[17:30] Alicia (Harbor): Regarding encryption at rest, do you use per-tenant keys or cluster keys? We want per-tenant isolation.
[17:37] Marco (Redwood): Dedicated/Private can do per-tenant keys. Hosted is typically cluster-level keys with envelope encryption per tenant; with BYOK you can get per-tenant control depending on the deployment. We'll document exact key scoping.

[20:00] Sofia (Redwood): On incident response — we can share our incident response playbook and mean time to detect/mitigate metrics. Also we do periodic pentests and vulnerability scans; we can share redacted summaries.
[20:19] Mei (Harbor): Good. We also require SOC2 subservice provider detail for major infra providers.
[20:27] Marco (Redwood): We include cloud provider SOC attestations and a list of subprocessors in the security pack we'll send.

[23:50] Rajesh (Harbor): A couple of edge questions — are model weights considered customer data? How is prompt/context data treated in logs and backups?
[24:05] Marco (Redwood): Prompt/content data is treated as customer data and is stored per the retention policy; for Hosted we log metadata but can redact or hash payloads on request. Model weights are part of the model artifact — for customer-provided models in Private deploys they remain in your environment. We'll include the data flow diagram.

[27:10] Sofia (Redwood): For compliance checks we can produce an audit bundle: access logs, config snapshots, and redacted request samples. That usually satisfies security teams.
[27:28] Alicia (Harbor): Great — that'll help speed our internal review.

[30:00] Marco (Redwood): Regarding RBAC, you can create fine-grained permissions (invoke, manage-models, view-billing, manage-keys). We'll map those to SCIM groups from your IdP.
[30:25] Rajesh (Harbor): Will actions by service accounts be identifiable? We rely on machine identity audits.
[30:32] Marco (Redwood): Yes, service accounts have their own principal and keys; their actions are logged with the principal ID.

[33:40] Mei (Harbor): A question about backups — if we request deletion under a retention policy, what's the guarantee/attestation for data erasure?
[33:50] Marco (Redwood): We support logical and physical deletion workflows depending on storage tier; for Hosted we provide deletion attestations and for Private you control the physical storage. We'll include the erasure procedure in the security pack.

[36:15] Sofia (Redwood): Ok, next practical step: We'll run a Dedicated pilot to validate latency, KMS flow, and retention exports. Marco will take the lead on the perf side.
[36:28] Marco (Redwood): I'll need a sample payload set, expected QPS, and desired latency SLOs. Also the list of regions and KMS provider.
[36:40] Rajesh (Harbor): I'll send sample payloads and QPS targets — we have a 500 RPS burst and steady 50 RPS.
[36:48] Marco (Redwood): Perfect. For the pilot we'll also configure logging export to your S3 so you can validate retention/archive.

[39:00] Alicia (Harbor): One more: data residency for backups — we need backups and audit logs stored in EU-only for some customers.
[39:08] Sofia (Redwood): Noted — we'll mark those constraints and see if Hosted region endpoints suffice or if Dedicated is needed.

[41:30] Mei (Harbor): On legal — our procurement team wants a DPA and clarity on liability caps. Who should they contact?
[41:36] Sofia (Redwood): I'll introduce you to our legal contact and send the standard DPA and SLA. Expect initial docs in the share by tomorrow.

[44:05] Rajesh (Harbor): Any gotchas with network peering for Private? We have strict routing rules and need to avoid public egress for model payloads.
[44:14] Marco (Redwood): Private can be deployed behind your network with direct peering and VPC-only egress; we'll run a design session with your network team.

[46:30] Sofia (Redwood): Recap — action items: Sofia sends SOC2/ISO and security pack; Marco runs Dedicated perf pilot; Harbor shares payloads and retention policy; legal to be looped for DPA. We'll follow up with scheduling links.
[46:50] Alicia (Harbor): Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[46:55] Mei (Harbor): Thanks.
[47:00] Sofia (Redwood): Thanks all, we'll get those docs over. Bye.

Notes on transcription quality: medium — a few words like "KV cache" were transcribed as "K V cash" in the automated text. There were short cross-talk moments.

End of meeting.
